title: Runtime compatibility shadowtest summary: flash-v2 + paged-kv + cont-batch
body:
Purpose:
This doc summarizes the shadow-test results for the combined runtime/kernel change that enables FlashAttention v2, swaps the paged-KV allocator, and tweaks the continuous-batching window heuristics. Goal was to detect functional/regression signal on our onboarding prompt sets and identify high-confidence mitigations before a rollout to dedicated clusters.

High-level takeaway (tl;dr):
- Enabling FlashAttention v2 + new paged-KV allocator produced negligible latency improvements (~3-6% P50) on most short-context traffic, but introduced two classes of behavioral regressions on long-context and structured-instruction prompts.
- Continuous-batching warmup reduction (batch window 25ms -> 10ms) reduced tail latency under load but increased token-level exposure to partial-prefix caching edge cases, leading to subtle token-skipping and KV-mismatch artifacts in ~0.4% of long-context generation samples.
- Overall risk is moderate: functional regressions are rare but non-random (clustered by prompt shape and attention pattern). Recommend hold/targeted rollout with mitigations rather than immediate full rollout.

Test setup and scope:
- Timeframe: 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-09 shadow runs.
- Models: rwd-base-13b (float16), rwd-instruct-7b-fp16.
- Configs compared:
  * baseline: FlashAttn v1, paged-kv-v2 (current prod), cont-batch window=25ms
  * candidate: FlashAttn v2, paged-kv-v3, cont-batch window=10ms
- Traffic: 120k shadowed requests across prompt buckets (see prompt partition below). Shadow routing mirrored responses; no user-facing change.
- Prompt partitions: short-chat (<=128 tokens), summarization (news/longdoc), code-assist (multi-turn), chain-of-thought (few-shot reasoning), config-instructions (structured tool-calling).
- Metrics collected: token-level logprob deltas, top-1 token mismatch rate, perplexity diff on held-out batches, semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) between baseline and candidate outputs, and a small human-eval rubric for hallucination/format violations on a stratified sample (n=1200).

Key quantitative diffs (candidate vs baseline):
- Short-chat: P50 latency -4.1%, P95 latency -1.2%; token-mismatch 0.06% (noise). Semantic sim 0.998 median. No human-eval regressions.
- Summarization (longdoc >2048 tokens): Perplexity +1.9% (worse), token-mismatch 0.8%, semantic sim 0.966; human-eval: 6/300 flagged for content omission or sentence reordering that changed meaning.
- Code-assist: Top-1 token mismatch 0.45%; observed truncated code-blocks in 4/200 samples (partial closing braces/missing indentation).
- Chain-of-thought: End-of-reasoning token dropouts in ~0.35% of runs; coherence score delta -0.04 (on 1-5 scale).
- Config-instructions (tool calling): Format-violation rate increased from 0.9% -> 2.1% (examples: missing JSON wrapper for tools, wrong field order causing downstream parsers to fail).

Observed failure modes (representative, with sample ids):
1) KV misalignment with repeated long-span prompts (sample id S-4821):
   - Symptom: model emitted a token sequence that repeated the last 64 tokens of the prefix in the middle of generation, producing duplicated paragraphs.
   - Root cause (hypothesis): paged-KV v3 allocator interacts with cont-batch early-eviction heuristic leading to stale KV pages being composed with a shifted index when continuous-batching merges partially overlapping in-flight requests.
   - Repro rate: ~0.7% on the affected long-context prompt shard.

2) Partial token emission during attention reordering (sample id C-229):
   - Symptom: code-assist responses missing final line of function; trailing newline present but closing token dropped.
   - Hypothesis: FlashAttn v2's fused kernel reorders micro-batches for memory locality and, combined with the smaller cont-batch window, causes an off-by-one in token commit for in-flight streams when the KV page boundary aligns with CUDA warp boundary.
   - Repro rate: 0.2% concentrated on code samples with very long input examples.

3) Structured output schema violations (sample id T-811):
   - Symptom: tool-calling JSON had top-level key name reordered and missing required action field (downstream parsers threw 400).
   - Notes: Mostly happens with instruction prompts containing several numbered examples; seems correlated with chain-of-thought style few-shot examples.

Diagnostics and triage steps performed:
- Replay tests with deterministic seeding reproduced 85% of flagged cases for the same model/config, confirming determinism for most failure classes.
- Performed binary ablations: FlashAttn v2 only (paged-kv baseline) and paged-kv v3 only (FlashAttn baseline). Results: paged-kv v3 alone accounts for most KV-duplication cases; FlashAttn v2 alone surfaces the token-drop edge cases in code-assist. The largest failure modes appear when both are combined under the tightened cont-batch window.
- Collected CUDA mem traces and page-fault logs on candidate nodes; found increased PM page churn on paged-kv v3 under steady long-context loads.
- Added extra logging to streaming commit pipeline; identified a timing edge where stream commit acknowledgement raced with KV page remap during merged batch flush.

Short human-eval notes (n=1200 stratified):
- Long-doc summarization regressions mostly reduce recall of details (minor omission) rather than hallucination. Priority: medium.
- Tooling schema violations are high-impact (failures are binary). Even a small percentage causes customer-visible errors. Priority: high.

Risk classification (candidate rollout risk):
- Safety/regression: medium-high for long-context structured workloads.
- Latency/Cost: small benefit on short traffic; negligible on long-context.
- Operational: medium — increased debug surface and potential for noisy errors in tool-calling paths.

Mitigation options and recommended immediate actions:
1) Hold full rollout. Implement targeted canary where:
   - FlashAttn v2 enabled only on short-context node pools (<=512 tokens).
   - Paged-KV v3 rolled to read-only on long-context pools (no eviction/repack) to validate allocator behavior.
   - Cont-batch window revert to 25ms for pools primarily serving long-context prompts.
   Owner: Jonah Martinez (eng-infra). ETA: 1 week for canary config.

2) Engineering fixes (parallel):
   - Patch paged-KV: add metadata fencing to prevent remap during in-flight stream commit. (Owner: Ravi Kapoor, ETA: 2w)
   - Add boundary-safe commit path in streaming service to serialize commit on KV page remap. (Owner: Lena Sørensen, ETA: 10d)
   - Add unit/regression tests: long-context replay harness with fuzzed page boundaries; extend CI to run small-scale FlashAttn v2 smoke tests against code-assist prompt set. (Owner: eng-applied-ml test lead, ETA: 1w)

3) Short-term runtime knobs:
   - Expose runtime flag to force cont-batch window per route and per model.
   - Add detection rule: when token-mismatch rate >0.25% for a route in shadow, automatically route that traffic to baseline kernel.

Action items (concrete):
- Aisha: draft PRD for staged rollout and incident playbook (due 2026-08-12).
- Jonah: configure short-context canary pools, enable enhanced logging (due 2026-08-14).
- Ravi/Lena: prioritize paged-KV fencing patch and streaming commit serialization; open change RFCs (due 2026-08-17).
- QA: create long-context fuzz harness and add to nightly (due 2026-08-20).

Appendix: prompt set notes and sample ids used in evaluation:
- prompt-bucket-short-chat: 41k requests; representative channels: customer-support, chat-widget.
- prompt-bucket-long-summ: 18k requests; included legal-docs, research-articles.
- prompt-bucket-code-assist: 32k requests; multi-turn examples from integration tests.
- prompt-bucket-cot: 17k requests; few-shot reasoning chains (~4 shots).
- sample ids: S-4821 (long-summ duplicate paragraph), C-229 (code truncation), T-811 (tool-json schema violation), B-3002 (benign mismatch example).

Notes to reviewers:
- Please focus review on the proposed staged rollout (are the canary constraints sufficient?) and the feasibility of the paged-KV fencing patch.
- If you have additional short-context pools we can use for early FlashAttn v2 traffic, add them to the comment thread in the linked PR.
- I left raw logs and sample replays in /mnt/shadow-logs/2026-08-07-09 for infra triage (internal path).
